content.comment_body: Hello. I'm looking for guidance on how to measure the duration an output remains high. I can trigger a timer when the output turns on, but I'm unsure how to detect when it turns off, stop the timer, record the elapsed time to the SD card, and reset for the next cycle. Since this event is infrequent, frequent SD card writes aren't a concern. Any advice would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

I've attached a basic example for reference. Please note that the stored value represents the total time counted by the stopwatch logic. For instance, if the time base is seconds and the output remains high for 2 minutes and 41 seconds, a value of 161 seconds will be logged in the data file.
This is very helpful—thank you. Using an edge NAND with a single input is a creative solution I hadn't considered. I appreciate your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking a dependable approach to record how long an output remains active, storing this data on an SD card for later review. The challenge lies in creating logic that can accurately detect state transitions, measure durations, reset for new cycles, and reduce unnecessary SD card writes. A clear, working example was provided, directly addressing the user's needs and improving their confidence in the approach.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates a simple and accurate method for detecting when an output turns on and off, measuring how long it stays high, and logging these times reliably to an SD card. The process should reset automatically to allow for repeated measurements.
